thread.title_full: Curious about Eastern WA data center plan? Amazon offering open house - NewsBreak

author: Wendy Culverwell
title: Curious about Eastern WA data center plan? Amazon offering open house - NewsBreak
text:
By Wendy Culverwell ,
13 hours ago An aerial view of an Amazon data center in Boardman, Ore., in 2022. Dave Killen/Courtesy The Oregonian Amazon Web Services officials will field questions in August about the company’s plan for a local data center as it works to secure permits.
AWS will hold a public open house from 4-8 p.m., Aug. 11, at Columbia High School, 787 Maple St., Burbank.
The open house is an opportunity to learn more about its proposed data center complex at Wallula Gap Business Park, southeast of Pasco in western Walla Walla County.
AWS operates data centers in Northeastern Oregon but had not previously targeted this area before 2024, when it cut a deal for the Port of Walla Walla property.
This spring, after closing the land deal, AWS submitted environmental review documents to Walla Walla County.
In June, however, the county said its application was incomplete without a traffic impact analysis. It has until Aug. 24 to complete the paperwork.
Amazon said the traffic review is complete and will be submitted after the open house.
Amazon Web Services will hold an open house in Burbank, Wash., to discuss its plan to build data centers at Wallula Gap Business Park, southeast of Pasco. Bob Brawdy/bbrawdy@tricityherald.com Amazon Web Services FAQ The company offered lengthy answers to data center questions in a series of FAQs posted to the Walla Walla County website.
AWS, initially operating behind the alias “Advance Phase LLC,” agreed to buy 500 acres from the port in 2024. It affirmed it identity in February , when it closed the $32 million deal.
It initiated the approval process when it filed an environmental review request, as required by Washington law.
The initial deal with the port indicated it would build up to 16 data centers on the 500-acre campus.
The potential investment of nearly $5 billion is a potential game changer for Walla Walla County, population 63,100. At the time, the combined value of all property was about $10 billion.
New documents indicate a smaller project, at least to start.
Amazon will build three, single-story data center buildings on 134 acres Each building will be about 220,000 square feet, about two-thirds the size of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool.
It will create 120 to 150 full-time jobs, AWS said.
The project also will include storage tanks, a security building and industrial water facility and a power substation.
The Port of Walla Walla will provide water and process water treatment services but not electricity.
Utility plans AWS said it uses water for cooling only 7% of the time and calculates the Wallula Gap complex will use 14 million gallons of water annually, less than a comparably sized irrigated farm circle.
While it did not specify the source of power for Wallula Gap, its FAQs note it is a major investor in green energy projects, including partnering with Energy Northwest on a small modular reactor complex known as Cascade Advanced Energy Facility north of Richland.
It confirmed it uses backup generators at its project sites.
The Tri-Cities is targeted for additional data center development by Atlas Agro North America (Richland), Trammel Crow Co. (West Richland) and the Pacific Northwest National Laboratory/DOE (Richland).
None have completed land deals for their sites or disclosed details.
